topic: Station operation and test equipment (G4A, G4B; 26 pool questions)

questions.question: What is the purpose of the notch filter found on many HF transceivers?

choices.A: To restrict the transmitter voice bandwidth
choices.B: To reduce interference from carriers in the receiver passband
choices.C: To eliminate receiver interference from impulse noise sources
choices.D: To remove interfering splatter generated by signals on adjacent frequencies

questions.answer: To reduce interference from carriers in the receiver passband

questions.question: What is the benefit of using the opposite or “reverse” sideband when receiving CW?

choices.A: Interference from impulse noise will be eliminated
choices.B: More stations can be accommodated within a given signal passband
choices.C: It may be possible to reduce or eliminate interference from other signals
choices.D: Accidental out-of-band operation can be prevented

questions.answer: It may be possible to reduce or eliminate interference from other signals

questions.question: How does a noise blanker work?

choices.B: By redirecting noise pulses into a filter capacitor
choices.C: By reducing receiver gain during a noise pulse

questions.answer: By reducing receiver gain during a noise pulse

questions.question: What is the effect on plate current of the correct setting of a vacuum-tube RF power amplifier’s TUNE control?

choices.B: A pronounced dip
choices.C: No change will be observed

questions.answer: A pronounced dip

questions.question: Why is automatic level control (ALC) used with an RF power amplifier?

choices.A: To balance the transmitter audio frequency response
choices.B: To reduce harmonic radiation
choices.C: To prevent excessive drive

questions.answer: To prevent excessive drive

questions.question: What is the purpose of an antenna tuner?

choices.A: Reduce the SWR in the feed line to the antenna
choices.B: Reduce the power dissipation in the feedline to the antenna
choices.C: Increase power transfer from the transmitter to the feed line

questions.answer: Increase power transfer from the transmitter to the feed line

questions.question: What happens as a receiver’s noise reduction control level is increased?

choices.B: Received frequency may become unstable
choices.C: CW signals may become severely attenuated
choices.D: Received frequency may shift several kHz

questions.answer: Received signals may become distorted

questions.question: What is the correct adjustment for the LOAD or COUPLING control of a vacuum tube RF power amplifier?

choices.B: Minimum plate current without exceeding maximum allowable grid current
choices.C: Highest plate voltage while minimizing grid current
choices.D: Desired power output without exceeding maximum allowable plate current

questions.answer: Desired power output without exceeding maximum allowable plate current

questions.question: What is the purpose of delaying RF output after activating a transmitter’s keying line to an external amplifier?

choices.A: To prevent key clicks on CW
choices.B: To prevent transient overmodulation
choices.C: To allow time for the amplifier to switch the antenna between the transceiver and the amplifier output
choices.D: To allow time for the amplifier power supply to reach operating level

questions.answer: To allow time for the amplifier to switch the antenna between the transceiver and the amplifier output

questions.question: What is the function of an electronic keyer?

choices.B: Automatic generation of dots and dashes for CW operation
choices.C: To allow time for switching the antenna from the receiver to the transmitter
choices.D: Computer interface for PSK and RTTY operation

questions.answer: Automatic generation of dots and dashes for CW operation

questions.question: Why should the ALC system be inactive when transmitting AFSK data signals?

choices.A: ALC will invert the modulation of the AFSK mode
choices.B: The ALC action distorts the signal
choices.C: When using digital modes, too much ALC activity can cause the transmitter to overheat

questions.answer: The ALC action distorts the signal

questions.question: Which of the following is a common use of the dual-VFO feature on a transceiver?

choices.A: To allow transmitting on two frequencies at once
choices.B: To permit full duplex operation -- that is, transmitting and receiving at the same time
choices.C: To transmit on one frequency and listen on another
choices.D: To improve frequency accuracy by allowing variable frequency output (VFO) operation

questions.answer: To transmit on one frequency and listen on another

questions.question: What is the purpose of using a receive attenuator?

choices.A: To prevent receiver overload from strong incoming signals
choices.B: To reduce the transmitter power when driving a linear amplifier
choices.C: To reduce power consumption when operating from batteries
choices.D: To reduce excessive audio level on strong signals

questions.answer: To prevent receiver overload from strong incoming signals

questions.question: What item of test equipment contains horizontal and vertical channel amplifiers?

choices.B: A signal generator
choices.C: An ammeter

questions.answer: An oscilloscope

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of an oscilloscope versus a digital voltmeter?

choices.B: Complex impedances can be easily measured
choices.C: Greater precision

questions.answer: Complex waveforms can be measured

questions.question: Which of the following is the best instrument to use for checking the keying waveform of a CW transmitter?

choices.B: A field strength meter
choices.C: A sidetone monitor

questions.answer: An oscilloscope

questions.question: What signal source is connected to the vertical input of an oscilloscope when checking the RF envelope pattern of a transmitted signal?

choices.A: The local oscillator of the transmitter
choices.B: An external RF oscillator
choices.C: The transmitter balanced mixer output
choices.D: The attenuated RF output of the transmitter

questions.answer: The attenuated RF output of the transmitter

questions.question: Why do voltmeters have high input impedance?

choices.B: It allows for higher voltages to be safely measured
choices.C: It improves the resolution of the readings
choices.D: It decreases the loading on circuits being measured

questions.answer: It decreases the loading on circuits being measured

questions.question: What is an advantage of a digital multimeter as compared to an analog multimeter?

choices.B: Less prone to overload
choices.C: Higher precision

questions.answer: Higher precision

questions.question: What signals are used to conduct a two-tone test?

choices.A: Two audio signals of the same frequency shifted 90 degrees
choices.B: Two non-harmonically related audio signals
choices.C: Two swept frequency tones
choices.D: Two audio frequency range square wave signals of equal amplitude

questions.answer: Two non-harmonically related audio signals

questions.question: What transmitter performance parameter does a two-tone test analyze?

choices.B: Percentage of suppression of the carrier and undesired sideband for SSB
choices.C: Percentage of frequency modulation

questions.answer: Linearity

questions.question: When is an analog multimeter preferred to a digital multimeter?

choices.B: When high precision is desired
choices.C: When measuring the frequency of an oscillator
choices.D: When adjusting circuits for maximum or minimum values

questions.answer: When adjusting circuits for maximum or minimum values

questions.question: Which of the following can be determined with a directional wattmeter?

choices.B: Antenna front-to-back ratio
choices.C: RF interference

questions.answer: Standing wave ratio

questions.question: Which of the following must be connected to an antenna analyzer when it is being used for SWR measurements?

choices.B: Transmitter
choices.C: Antenna and feed line

questions.answer: Antenna and feed line

questions.question: What effect can strong signals from nearby transmitters have on an antenna analyzer?

choices.A: Desensitization which can cause intermodulation products which interfere with impedance readings
choices.B: Received power that interferes with SWR readings
choices.C: Generation of harmonics which interfere with frequency readings

questions.answer: Received power that interferes with SWR readings

questions.question: Which of the following can be measured with an antenna analyzer?

choices.B: Power output from a transmitter
choices.C: Impedance of coaxial cable

questions.answer: Impedance of coaxial cable
